Stated Claim / Post Context:
Opinion: A China without religious freedom is a China we cannot do business with

Faith belongs to the faithful souls, not the government.

Actual Article Body:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington last week brought renewed attention to the U.S.-China relationship. The meeting should have also drawn attention to the millions in China who face government pressure because of how they worship.

This year, Americans of all backgrounds celebrated 250 years of a nation founded on the freedoms to think, worship, speak and govern themselves freely. Our history reminds us that religious liberty cannot be taken for granted. It must be protected in families, congregations, schools and communities — and defended wherever governments seek to suppress it.

Men and women of faith in China face a powerful government determined to place their deepest beliefs under political control.

Under Xi Jinping, Beijing has intensified its campaign to “Sinicize” religion, forcing faith communities to conform their teachings, leadership and institutions to Communist Party ideology.

The consequences can be seen across China.
